name: Global temperature
summary: Global temperature 1.83°C above pre-industrial on 9 Nov, a record for the date
state: ERA5 data for 9 Nov put global surface air temperature at 14.55°C, about 1.83°C above pre-industrial levels and a record for the calendar date, above the 1.6°C Alert line (Climate Reanalyzer). The estimate adds 0.88°C to the 1991–2020 anomaly of 0.95°C. Readings have held above about 1.8°C since late October, with the very strong El Niño adding heat.
for_you: Record warmth raises the odds of heatwaves, heavy rain and marine heat stress. Follow national weather service warnings where you live.

sources.title: Climate Reanalyzer — Daily global surface air temperature (ERA5)

why: Global temperature is the master climate variable; each tenth of a degree raises extreme-weather risk.
drivers: Greenhouse gases, El Niño/La Niña, aerosols, solar cycle.

rubric.alert: > +1.6°C, or a record high for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Daily global anomaly < +1.3°C above pre-industrial (ERA5 vs 1991–2020 + 0.88°C).
